To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a simple combination of low-level image processing, temporal Fourier analysis and contour detection can be used to provide rapid and robust LV localization in 4D cardiac MRI.

we have developed a method for automatic LV localization and orientation that can be applied to 4D CMRs and that is robust and accurate enough to provide rapid and reliable feedback for automated scan-planning or further processing.

a novel combination of low-level image processing and anatomical knowledge can be applied to automatically locate and orient the LV in a large study population of 4D CMRs, with errors comparable to those made in manual planning by experienced technicians, and that the proposed method can provide rapid, robust and accurate feedback for scan planning or further analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an automatic method for the detection of LV in 4D CMRs.
the development of methods for the analysis of cardiac magnetic resonance (MR) data.
the development of an automated method for detection of the left ventricular cavity in 4D CMRI.

this method is a very promising tool for the automated detection of the LV in 4D CMRs.
the automated method is able to accurately localize and orientate the LV in CMR data, and that this is robust to a range of disease states.
the method presented is a fast, robust, and accurate way of locating the LV in a 4D CMRI dataset.

we have developed a fully automated, fast and accurate method to detect the location of the left ventricular in 4D CMRs.
we have presented a fully automated method that is able to localize the left ventracle in a 4D cardiac magnetic resonance dataset without user intervention, which is accurate, robust and fast.
